method: Reconstructed after the fact, not recorded at run time. Each campaign is a uniquely-named profile introduced by exactly one commit; the configs-<profile>/ files were written locally by gen_configs.py on the same clock as git commit, so their mtimes anchor the campaign to that commit. Corroborated where possible by config content, run.log feature fingerprints, and EXPERIMENTS.md prose.

profile_commit.subject: feat: add TLSF mono-vs-muc mutation-split campaign (profile muc, sweep M)

profile_commit_evidence: Configs written 33 seconds before the commit; runs begin 10 minutes later.
binary_commit_note: Not inferable. Binaries on av2/av3 lag main by an unbounded, undocumented amount, so a commit falling inside a run window may be absent from the binary that ran. 62bbc6f is the standing proof: committed 2026-07-20 14:16, squarely inside the muc run window, yet EXPERIMENTS.md records it as not in that campaign's binary. Do not derive binary attribution from window containment. Campaigns run after the --version change carry a recorded binary commit in their manifest instead.

run_window.note: Run-window mtimes come from two hosts with unsynced clocks; av3 runs ~17 min fast. Seeds partition by host (av2 low, av3 high), so the run dir name identifies which clock a timestamp came from.

recorded_binary_facts.subject: fix: bound and reap the ltl2tgba model-counting subprocess
recorded_binary_facts.fact: EXPERIMENTS.md: "The fix - a counting-path timeout plus `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` on every subprocess - landed after this campaign (not in the binary it ran), so the humanoid timing carries some leak noise." Corroborated by run.log fingerprints: earliest and latest runs have identical report structure and zero timeout annotations, so no rebuild occurred mid-campaign. This is the decisive counterexample to inferring binary content from run-window containment: the commit timestamp falls inside this window.

caveats: Directory is named 07-21 (archive date) but the campaign ran from 07-17.
